blocks.text: The curator's daily struggle with collection management software

Your day is split between high level research and the reality of data entry. You might use TMS, EMu, or Axiell Collections to keep track of thousands of objects. These systems are powerful but often require dozens of clicks to reach a specific record. This friction adds up over a long afternoon of cataloging.

When you use Lazur, you can ask where a specific field is located. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask, "Where is the condition report field in this window?" Lazur will draw a circle around the exact spot. You do not need to hunt through submenus or read manual pages. You keep your eyes on the object and your hands on the keyboard.

Most curators feel the weight of administrative tasks. You are often the registrar, the researcher, and the donor liaison all at once. This constant switching between roles creates mental fatigue. Lazur helps by handling the small, repetitive actions that pull you away from your research.

If you need to draft an email to a donor or update a project status in Notion, use the dictation feature. Hold the fn key and speak your notes. Lazur types them out cleanly at your cursor. It handles names and technical terms well. This keeps you in your creative zone rather than typing out repetitive status updates.
Research and documentation on your Mac

Research often requires keeping dozens of browser tabs open. You might be comparing provenance records across multiple archives. Lazur can help you summarize web pages using the research capability. It works in the background so you can continue working in your primary collection management software.

When you have a question about how to perform a task in a new version of your software, ask Lazur to guide you. It will walk you through the steps one click at a time. It waits for you to finish each action before moving to the next. This is helpful when you are learning a new feature or a complex workflow.

Museum work involves sensitive data, including donor information and loan agreements. You must always follow your employer's rules regarding data privacy. Lazur is designed with this in mind. It does not store your screen images or audio recordings. It only sees what you show it while you hold the activation key.

You should treat Lazur as a tool to help you work faster, not as a replacement for your professional judgment. It does not click buttons or edit your files. It only points and explains. You remain in full control of every update to your collections database.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my specific collection management software?
faq.answer: Lazur works with any application on your Mac. Because it uses visual recognition, it can help you navigate web-based systems like Axiell or desktop-based tools without needing a direct integration.

faq.question: Is my museum data safe when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur does not store your screen content or audio. It processes your request only while you hold the shortcut key and does not use your data to train AI models.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my database records for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, type in fields, or change data. It guides you, points to things on the screen, and answers your questions so you can do the work yourself.
